lines.text: As a teenager, he lined up for food stamps.
Years later, he signed a nineteen billion dollar deal.
Jan Koum grew up in Ukraine and moved to California at sixteen with his mother.
They were so poor they lived on government help. He swept floors in a grocery store.
He taught himself to program and got a job at Yahoo.
In 2009, he built a simple app to send messages over the internet.
No ads, no games, just messages. He called it WhatsApp.
Within five years, hundreds of millions of people were using it.
In 2014, Facebook bought it for about nineteen billion dollars. The company had just fifty-five employees.
And he signed the deal on the door of the old welfare office where he once collected food stamps.
Follow for more true stories of fortunes made and lost.
